task.name: Fix Mac app Agent activity banner: activity --json decode misses `aggregate` key
task.description:
Fix Mac app Agent activity banner: activity --json decode misses `aggregate` key

The Mac app ([Loopflow.app](<http://Loopflow.app>) 0.12.8) shows a persistent warning banner in the Wave Fleet header:

> Agent activity unavailable
> lf query JSON did not decode: keyNotFound(CodingKeys(stringValue: "aggregate", intValue: nil), Swift.DecodingError.Context(codingPath: [], debugDescription: "No value associated with key CodingKeys(stringValue: "aggregate", intValue: nil)")

Where it happens:

* swift/Loopflow/Services/RegistryQuery.swift:349 throws RegistryQueryError("lf query JSON did not decode: ...").
* The failing call is the activity query: `workActivity(...)` runs `lf activity --since ... --limit ... --json` and decodes `WorkActivitySnapshot` (RegistryQuery.swift:120-133). The Swift DTO requires a top-level `aggregate` key that the CLI's `lf activity --json` payload does not emit (or emits under a different shape).

This is wire-DTO drift between the Swift mirror and the Rust emitter. Per STYLE.md's DTO rules: no defaults, every field required or explicitly Optional, and round-trip fixtures under tests/fixtures/dto/ must cover the shape.

Done when:

* `lf activity --json` output and the Swift `WorkActivitySnapshot` DTO agree on the wire shape (decide whether `aggregate` is required from the CLI or removed/Optional in Swift — align with what the Rust side actually emits and the fixture).
* The DTO fixture under tests/fixtures/dto/ covers the reconciled shape and both language fixture tests pass.
* The Mac app renders agent activity with no "Agent activity unavailable" banner against the live `lf` 0.12.8+ CLI.

task.name: See and control all current and available work from the Mac
task.description:
Design: scratch/w2-141.md (W2-141). Depends on the lf work read command.

One query, two shapes — a lens may change the SHAPE, not merely filter one outline:

NOW — flat, cross-wave, grouped by attention (Ready for review, Needs input, Working, Stopped, Failed), ordered by age within each group. Rows carry wave/project as context, not as structure. This is what Claude Codes agent view arrived at, and what Conductor (the healthiest worktree manager) uses: a status-grouped list, not lanes.

ROADMAP — the Wave > Project > Task tree from the PM snapshot. Complete, and renderable with zero processes running. Projects collapse to KR proof plus a session census; waves collapse to residency plus an attention count. synced_at always on screen.

Every row carries three orthogonal facts on independent channels, never collapsed into one status word: PM completion, Session status, and process liveness. A dead process is not a dead task — a Stopped row stays attachable and resumable and says why it stopped.

Swift work:

* [RegistryQuery.work](<http://RegistryQuery.work>)() -> lf work --json -> WorkSnapshot. Replaces the per-wave lf pm show fan-out in WavesView.buildWavePlanCache (one spawn, not N).
* WaveProjectWork / WaveTaskWork already mirror the per-wave shape and runtime is already Optional, so the Available predicate decodes today.
* Delete RegistryQuery.backlog() and BacklogItem. backlog() computes availability as !completed over lf pm show, which carries no Session data; its docstring tells callers to "subtract running task ids/titles" — a title-matched join. It has no production callers. Availability is the ABSENCE of a Session, not a PM property.

No kanban board. The board metaphor is losing empirically (Vibe Kanban sunsetting, Crystal deprecated, Terragon shut down), and a board whose drag does nothing is a lie.

Ineligible rows are greyed WITH THE REASON attached, never hidden — OmniFocus stacks a computed availability model and a per-view filter with different semantics, and produced years of "where did my task go" threads. One hiding mechanism, never two.

HOME CONTROL — depends on W2-88 as well as lf work

Each Loopflow Wave has one inherited Home. Show that address on its Wave or product row and consume shared Home runtime evidence without implementing SSH in Swift. The surface distinguishes unreachable, unknown, reachable but stopped, and running. Selecting the Home navigates or opens the correct execution context. The primary contextual action is Open or Attach when running, Start on <home> when reachable but stopped, and an actionable reason when it cannot be reached. Start is idempotent, runs on the configured Home rather than the UI machine, and returns the resident identity needed to attach. The same Home, state, reason, and controls must appear in CLI status and the shared DTO; no Mac-only lifecycle model.

A podium-review screenshot job left `Google Chrome --headless=new --no-startup-window --screenshot=scratch/podium-review/html-mobile.png --user-data-dir=/tmp/loopflow-podium-mobile.D8pMr8` running orphaned (ppid 1) for 5h37m on 2026-08-19. task.name: [absorbed] Fix Chrome focus stealing and login-server teardown
task.description:
Hotfix lf auth connect: stop 1 Hz Chrome focus-stealing and the 180s login-server teardown

Two defects in the managed login ceremony (`lf auth connect`), observed live on 0.12.8 while reconnecting accounts. Both block account recovery, which blocks wave/project runners fleet-wide.

Defect 1 — focus stealing (claude path):
`capture_claude_authorization_code_from_chrome` (rust/loopflow/src/provider_auth/mod.rs:1828) polls in a loop until CLAUDE_BROWSER_AUTH_TIMEOUT, executing CLAUDE_VISIBLE_PAGE_SCRIPT ([mod.rs:1864](<http://mod.rs:1864>)) every 1 second. Each iteration unconditionally runs:

* `tell application "Google Chrome" to activate` — yanks Chrome to the foreground every second, regardless of whether the auth window exists yet
* `perform action "AXRaise"` + synthesized `keystroke "a"/"c" using command down` — Cmd+A/Cmd+C land in whatever the user is typing in if focus shifts mid-delay
* clipboard save/restore each poll — races with any user copy during the ceremony

The user cannot use their machine while the ceremony runs. Fix direction: never `activate` in the poll loop. Query window existence passively (System Events window enumeration needs no activation); only when the matching "Authentication code | Claude Platform (<profile>)" window is present, do one activate+raise+copy pass. Better still, prefer reading the page without synthetic keystrokes if Chrome scripting allows.

Defect 2 — premature login-server teardown (codex path, reproduced today):
`connect` for authorization flows waits `tokio::time::timeout(AUTH_STATUS_POLL_TIMEOUT, handle.wait())` with AUTH_STATUS_POLL_TIMEOUT = 180s (lf/commands/auth.rs:36,379). On timeout, lf exits; the `.login-` tempdir drops and the AuthProcessGroup Drop (provider_auth/mod.rs:1798) SIGKILLs the codex login process group — including its localhost:1455 OAuth callback listener. A user still completing browser login then gets redirected to [http://localhost:1455/auth/callback?](<http://localhost:1455/auth/callback?>)... and sees ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED (reproduced 2026-08-19 with [manabot-eng@loopflow.studio](<mailto:manabot-eng@loopflow.studio>); nothing listening on 1455 afterward). The authorization code is orphaned and the account stays credential_state=missing.

180 seconds is far too short for a real login (password manager, 2FA, SSO redirects), and there is no env/config override (`wait_for_active_status` only honors provider expires_in). Fix direction: for interactive browser confirmation, wait the authorization-code flow window (AUTH_CODE_FLOW_TIMEOUT_SECS = 600 exists already at [auth.rs:40](<http://auth.rs:40>)) or until Ctrl-C, and print a clear "still waiting for browser approval (Ns elapsed)" heartbeat so the user knows the listener is alive.

Done when:

* During a claude connect ceremony, Chrome is activated at most once before the auth window exists and once to harvest the code; the user can type in another app for the entire poll window without losing focus or keystrokes (manual demo on macOS).
* A codex connect survives a slow login: with approval deliberately delayed past 3 minutes, the localhost callback still lands, the account flips to connected, and `lf usage` shows it. Reproduce the old behavior's failure in a test at the timeout boundary if feasible without a live provider.
* `lf auth connect codex manabot-eng@loopflow.studio` completes on this machine (the account invalidated since Aug 14 — the live victim).

<!-- loopflow-task-start:64e413e9cfa527f6343ffd7659325757a2419f5b7bee089b2072418bc5955d3b -->

## Consolidation

Absorbed into LOO-223. LOO-223 owns both bounded headless-Chrome capture lifetime and the authentication focus/callback acceptance cases from this Task.

task.name: Make release upgrades converge on an always-on Home
task.description:
# 5 Whys: An always-on Home cannot install a migration-bearing release

## The Problem

Installing the latest published release was refused because nine Runs were
non-ended, but an always-on Loopflow Home may never naturally reach zero Runs.

## Chain

Always-on Home cannot update -> every non-ended Run blocks migration -> install
has no quiesce/resume protocol -> the safety fix assumed a manual zero-Run
window -> installation is modeled as file replacement rather than Home
reconciliation.

**Problem**: The machine remained on `lf 0.12.4` while the Product demo needed
the `0.12.5` store frontier. Installing the published `v0.12.5` artifact found
nine active or stopping Runs and changed nothing.

**Why 1**: A migration-bearing promotion rejects every Run whose durable state
is not `ended`; the check does not mean an old process is currently writing.

**Why 2**: The installer can fence new Run reservations, but it cannot ask
resident Work to checkpoint, drain its process containment, or resume afterward.

**Why 3**: Promotion was hardened after a branch binary was installed behind an
incompatible shared-store frontier. The prevention correctly fails closed, but
its only safe state is a manually drained machine.

**Why 4**: At that point Loopflow did not have sufficiently durable desired
on/off state and restart reconciliation to preserve user intent through a
coordinated control-plane restart.

**Why 5 (Root)**: Updating Loopflow is treated as replacing CLI/daemon/app files
plus migrating SQLite, not as a Home operation that converges enabled Work onto
a new runtime generation.

## Unanswered Whys

| Branch Point | Unexplored Question | Priority |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Why 1 | Which non-ended Runs have live old-code containment, and which are only durable pursuit state? | High |
| Why 2 | What is the safe checkpoint boundary for Wave, Project, and Task Runs? | High |
| Why 3 | Which release migrations can remain backward-compatible for a rolling upgrade? | Medium |
| Why 4 | How should remote Homes coordinate a fleet update without a global outage? | Medium |

## Fixes

| Level | Fix | Prevents |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Immediate | Make the normal production updater download and promote the latest published artifact, exactly like an external install; keep current-main builds dev-local. | Maintainers accidentally treating unreleased `main` as production. |
| Structural | Add a migration upgrade operation that fences new Runs, checkpoints and drains live containment, promotes and migrates, then reconciles enabled Work. | Requiring a human to manufacture a zero-Run window. |
| Systemic | Treat runtime generation and upgrade state as Home reconciliation facts with durable receipts and restart policy. | Always-on operation and safe upgrades remaining contradictory goals. |

## Changes to Implement

- [ ] Replace main-pulling production refresh with latest-published-release
  resolution and the same signed-artifact promotion path external users take.
- [ ] Preserve an explicit dev-only source-build command that cannot become the
  production runtime while migration drafts exist.
- [ ] Distinguish durable non-ended Work from live old-generation process
  containment in promotion evidence.
- [ ] Persist Home upgrade intent and block new Run reservations for the old
  generation.
- [ ] Checkpoint and stop live Wave, Project, and Task bodies without changing
  their enabled flags, definitions, worktrees, or PM state.
- [ ] Promote CLI, daemon, and app; advance the migration frontier; restart the
  Home; reconcile every enabled Work item.
- [ ] Emit a typed receipt for drain, migration, restart, resumed Work, timeout,
  and rollback/failure state.
- [ ] Prove a migration-bearing release on an active Wave/Project/Task fixture
  resumes the same Work without an operator-created zero-Run window.

task.name: Make LLM-session checkpoints authoritative for Task landing
task.description:
## Problem

Managed Task work currently teaches two incompatible human surfaces. LOOPFLOW.md presents `lf pr submit` plus a GitHub merge click as the human shipping gate, while the Task lifecycle already creates durable interactive reviews inside provider-backed LLM sessions.

The lifecycle model is broader than one final Gate. Any `interactive: true` step in Kickoff, Iterate, or Gate may use `InteractionPolicy::Require` and block on a human in the existing LLM transcript. `Defer` assigns that same exercise to the owning Project LLM session. Therefore require/require/require, require/defer/require, and defer/defer/defer are all legitimate authored policies; they are not migration states to normalize.

GitHub UI review and a human merge click duplicate this model without its evidence, phase ownership, changes-requested transition, or recovery semantics. Conversely, arming `land` during Iterate can let merge outrun later required LLM-session checkpoints.

## User-visible outcome

A human conducts every required Task checkpoint by conversing in an LLM session, whether the checkpoint appears during Kickoff, Iterate, or Gate. The Task remains parked at that exact lifecycle step until the durable InteractionReview disposition resolves it. Project-deferred checkpoints happen through the Project LLM session using the same review protocol.

Managed Tasks never require the GitHub UI for review or merge. Agents publish PRs as evidence while work is in flight. Once the Task lifecycle has cleared every applicable required interaction, its approved settlement intent still matches current Task and PR evidence, and repository checks permit merging, Loopflow lands the PR mechanically. `changes-requested` resumes the correct owning phase without merge.

`submit` and `pr open` remain available only outside managed Tasks or when a human explicitly asks to inspect GitHub; neither is part of the managed Task lifecycle.

## End-to-end proof

Exercise managed Tasks against a real test repository and shared store:

1. A required Kickoff interaction parks in the Task provider transcript. Human follow-ups stay FIFO in that transcript; approval advances and changes-requested does not silently skip the Kickoff checkpoint.
2. A Task whose Iterate plan is `Require` parks on an interactive inner-flow step and cannot publish settlement or arm merge until that review resolves. A `Defer` Iterate routes the same exercise to the Project provider transcript.
3. Required Gate interactions run in the Task provider transcript. Changes-requested returns the same Session to Iterate; approval permits settlement only when the reviewed fingerprint remains current.
4. No managed path opens GitHub or waits for a human merge click. Iterate may call `lf pr publish`; `lf pr submit` and premature `lf pr land` are refused or excluded from Task prompts before lifecycle approval.
5. After all required lifecycle reviews clear, one replay-safe landing uses the recorded `-c` or `--next <slug>` disposition. CI failure keeps the PR open and invokes the existing repair lifecycle; green CI lets the merge queue settle it.
6. Restart during an LLM review or between final approval and land preserves the transcript, phase, disposition, and exactly-once landing action.

Prove this with focused Task runner/store/PR-operation tests and a CLI-level lifecycle exercise spanning required Kickoff, required Iterate, required Gate, changes-requested, restart, approval, and merge.

## Source of truth

The authoritative state is TaskLifecyclePlan and its per-phase InteractionPolicy, the phase cursor, durable InteractionReview conversation/disposition/evidence, TaskGateProposal settlement intent, and TaskPr publication/after-merge disposition. LLM prompts, CLI/Mac status, and recommended actions are derived views. GitHub review state is repository evidence, not human lifecycle authority.

## Affected surfaces and consumers

* Task runner transitions and review resumption in Kickoff, Iterate, and Gate
* Human and Project reviewer protocols in the existing provider-backed transcripts
* TaskGateProposal and TaskPr settlement intent, including replay-safe complete-versus-next landing
* Task-worktree authority for `lf pr publish`, `submit`, `open`, and `land`
* LOOPFLOW.md; task_clarify, task_pursue, task_mutate, review-design, demo, code-review, gate, land, and submit skills
* `lf task attach`, review message/reply/complete commands, Mac handoff presentation, status, and recommended actions
* CLI help, README, operations documentation, builtin prompt assertions, and lifecycle tests

## Absent and error states

No live provider body, missing reviewer, unresolved required review, changes-requested, stale evidence fingerprint, changed PR head, no PR, missing settlement disposition, CI failure, GitHub outage, failed land request, restart, and missing registry authority must each produce an actionable durable state. None may silently advance a phase, self-approve, open GitHub as a fallback, merge early, duplicate land, or wait on an unexplained merge click.

## Operational boundary

Review conversations and dispositions survive body replacement. Approval-to-land is replay safe across process death and network failure. The system never arms merge while any required lifecycle review is unresolved or while reviewed Task/PR evidence is stale.

## Exclusions

Do not remove GitHub PRs, weaken branch protection, eliminate `submit` for ordinary non-Task PRs, require one fixed interaction policy across all phases, add policy-selection UI, or redesign the generic provider terminal transport.

## Project KR

Directly advances: every dispatched task loop either lands its PR unattended after its LLM-session checkpoints clear or stops with an actionable non-convergence record, with zero silent stalls and zero human rescues through GitHub.

```bash
cargo test -p loopflow --test land_tests submit_refuses_a_managed_task_before_any_mutation
```

Make the Task `finally` review the sole human shipping decision. Managed Tasks now reject `lf pr submit`, removing the redundant GitHub merge click while preserving `submit` for ordinary PRs.

The existing `finally` gate, exact-head merge pin, and durable merge request remain the shipping authority. No explicit separation-of-duties policy exists for managed Tasks today; ordinary non-Task PRs retain that workflow.

- Resolve Task authority and validate the PR range first, then reject managed `submit` before the first push, any `gh pr` mutation, or PR-copy generation.

- Update user docs, builtin operational guidance, and prompt goldens to teach one Task shipping sequence.

task.name: [retired] Make OpenCode GLM SSE disconnects observable and recoverable
task.description:
User-visible outcome

Product Wave work can use GLM through OpenCode without producing a hollow body. If OpenCode's SSE stream disconnects before useful work or mid-turn, Loopflow records the exact failure, preserves the durable Session/directive/worktree, and either retries only at a proven-safe boundary or hands the next body to the configured backup provider. No body that emitted no usable work remains reported as healthy or complete.

Incident evidence

During the current Product pursuit, several GLM/OpenCode bodies were hollow after an SSE disconnect. The work had to be handed manually to Claude Opus. Preserve the affected run/process/Task receipts as the reproduction corpus; do not infer the cause from the provider name alone.

Investigation and contract

* Identify where the SSE stream ended: OpenCode/provider transport, Loopflow harness decoding, timeout/cancellation, or account/model routing. Record model, provider, endpoint class, timing, last valid event, and terminal error without logging credentials or raw auth.
* Define an observable hollow-body boundary: no incorporated directive, durable mutation, useful assistant output, or explicit terminal disposition.
* Make pre-first-content and mid-stream disconnects produce durable failed/stalled body evidence with an actionable reason. Never turn EOF into success.
* Preserve Task/Project Session identity, provider history, worktree, commands, and generation fencing across recovery.
* Retry only when replay safety is proven. Otherwise route the next generation through the configured backup provider and retain the failed OpenCode generation as audit evidence.
* Keep the behavior in the shared OpenCode/harness and child-supervision contract, not Product-specific prompts or a GLM-name special case.

Proof

* A deterministic fake SSE server covers disconnect before headers/content, after metadata but before useful output, mid-tool call, and after a durable completion event.
* Tests prove exact body outcome, no false completion, one writer, no duplicate external side effect, and correct safe retry or backup-provider handoff.
* Replay the affected Product receipts and explain the root cause from evidence.
* Run at least ten GLM/OpenCode Product bodies with zero hollow successes; every forced disconnect is visible with reason and recovery owner.

Linear Task: [LOO-207](https://linear.app/loopflow/issue/LOO-207/make-managed-tasks-survive-missing-lifecycle-flows)

## Try it!

```bash
cargo test -p loopflow --lib resident_records_an_invalid_lifecycle_once_without_retrying
cargo test -p loopflow --lib lost_body_parks_an_invalid_lifecycle_without_relaunching
cargo test -p loopflow --lib repaired_persisted_task_flows_validate_through_the_generic_path
```

The first proof runs two resident ticks and observes one resumable failure event,
zero Runs, and one unchanged PR. The second proves the lost-body path stops at
the same boundary. The third verifies that the released historical migration
still repairs the recorded LOO-167, LOO-193, and LOO-195 shapes from `task` to
`slice`.

Before: every Project supervision tick could attempt the same invalid lifecycle
recovery again. After: the first tick writes one actionable receipt; later ticks
write no event, reserve no Run, create no PR, and emit no repeated warning.

## Intent

Make unavailable Task lifecycle flows converge durably. Resident supervision
now validates the persisted plan before PR reconciliation or relaunch, records
the exact refusal once, and parks until the named flow becomes valid again.


## Assumptions

- One active Project supervisor owns each Task recovery loop.
- The v0.12.5 `repair_legacy_task_flow` migration remains the sole historical
  `task → slice` data repair.
- Current Task lifecycle selections are immutable; unknown invalid pins are
  restored in place or the Task is abandoned and replaced.

## Key decisions

- Reuse the launch validator instead of creating resident-only flow rules.
- Persist one resumable Task failure so status and supervision share durable
  evidence.
- Compare the exact latest error and warn only when first recording it.
- Stop before Run reservation, PR rotation, or provider launch.

## Not included

- Compatibility flow aliases or runtime flow-name migration.
- Automatic worktree reconstruction.
- Changes to Project or Wave lifecycle recovery.

task.description:
## User-visible outcome

An agent can deliberately open an interactive Codex, Claude Code, or other vendor session in the correct Home and worktree, block behind that exact session, and resume after the human completes or hands the work back. task.name: Make Wave control-plane reconciliation self-healing
task.description:
## User-visible outcome

A running Wave continuously converges durable Project and Task intent with live process bodies, provider work, pull-request truth, and repository state. Users no longer see dead Projects counted as active, merged PRs described as open, or read-only commands rewriting their canonical checkout. After a laptop restart or body death, Loopflow either safely recovers the same work or names the exact boundary requiring intervention.

## Evidence to investigate

1. A live Product or Infrastructure Wave resident did not recover dead Project bodies.
2. Product reported five active Projects while every Project process was dead.
3. W2-135 continued to report PR #903 as open after GitHub had merged it.
4. Read-only Project turns refused to run when canonical main was dirty.
5. lf wt list invoked sync_main, auto-stashed existing edits, updated canonical main, and still returned a listing; additional edits then made main dirty again.

Preserve these as five deterministic reproductions. Do not collapse them into one generic stale-status bug before the ownership and event paths are mapped.

## Research questions

* Which durable record expresses desired Wave, Project, and Task intent, and which supervisor owns convergence for each level?
* What does active mean for intent, Session, body, provider turn, and child work? Which counts and labels should each product surface expose?
* Which event or observation reconciles GitHub PR state, and how fresh must it be before status may claim open, merged, failed, or review-required?
* Why do read-only Project turns depend on a clean mutable canonical checkout? Can they run against an immutable recorded base or repository snapshot while Task writers retain isolated worktrees?
* Which commands currently call sync_main or other mutating Git operations transitively? What public API makes read-only versus synchronizing behavior mechanically explicit?
* Which failures belong to automatic recovery, safe adoption, retry, NeedsInput, or terminal state under the W2-135 lease model?

## Source of truth

Durable Wave, Project, Task, directive, PR-sequence, and body-generation records in the Loopflow store own intent and identity. Process probes, GitHub, Git, and provider sessions are timestamped observations, not alternate identity. One reconciliation projection derives status, active counts, attention, next owner, and legal controls for CLI, roadmap, chat, and Swift.

## Product and API contract

* A live Wave supervisor periodically and eventfully reconciles every selected Project Session. It adopts a valid body, starts a safe missing body, preserves terminal intent, or records why recovery is unsafe.
* Desired active intent and observed live bodies are distinct typed fields. Counts must state which they count; a dead body can never make a live-process count positive.
* PR observations reconcile by stable PR identity and current head. A merge transitions the PR sequence exactly once and wakes the owning Project or Task decision path without waiting for a manual status probe.
* Read-only Project turns and inspection commands never require, clean, sync, reset, stash, fetch into, or rewrite canonical main. If fresh upstream state is required, the command names and owns that mutation explicitly.
* lf wt list and every other list, status, roadmap, doctor, diff, and file inspection surface are side-effect free. Add a mechanical command classification or boundary test so future transitive sync calls fail review and CI.
* Reconciliation is idempotent and restart-safe. Concurrent Wave, Project, Task, status, and external-observer events converge without duplicate bodies, lost edits, repeated PR transitions, or parallel intent.
* Every automatic action and refusal emits durable evidence with reason, freshness, next owner, and legal controls, feeding W2-123 rather than inventing a second presentation model.

## Affected surfaces and consumers

Wave and Project supervisors; Task/PR lifecycle; store schema and events; GitHub observation; Git/worktree operations; lf status, lf roadmap, lf project/task status, lf wt list, lf doctor; Wave Chat; Mac and iOS shared DTOs; builtin Wave/Project/Task skills; release and dogfood automation.

## Absent and error states

Missing execution context, unavailable GitHub, unreachable Home, ambiguous process ownership, dirty canonical checkout, stale observations, uncertain external side effects, and conflicting generations must remain explicit evidence. Never guess, report an empty healthy state, mutate main during inspection, or replay a control-uncertain action.

## Operational boundary

Reconciliation must remain bounded with no provider body required for mechanical adoption, liveness, GitHub refresh, or status projection. Read-only local commands should return promptly from persisted evidence and bounded probes. GitHub failure preserves the last observation with its age. A restart must converge without a human discovering the stall first.

## End-to-end proof

Run Product and Infrastructure with at least two selected Projects each. Kill every Project body, merge one waiting Task PR externally, leave canonical main dirty with named uncommitted edits, and invoke wt list, status, roadmap, and Project reconciliation concurrently. Prove:

* the Wave residents recover every replay-safe Project body exactly once;
* live-body and durable-intent counts remain distinct and correct;
* the merged PR advances once and reaches its owning decision path;
* all inspection commands leave HEAD, index, worktree, refs, and stash byte-for-byte unchanged;
* unsafe recovery becomes NeedsInput with exact evidence;
* CLI and Swift fixtures render the same state, reason, freshness, owner, and controls.

Repeat the scenario across process and laptop restart. Re-running reconciliation is a no-op.

## Delivery shape

One stable Task worktree and ordered serial PRs. Begin with a cross-layer design and deterministic reproductions. Expected slices are: reconciliation/source-of-truth model; Project-body recovery and active-count semantics; PR observation convergence; side-effect-free inspection and explicit sync APIs; shared status consumers and real two-Wave dogfood. Adjust boundaries when the code proves a simpler sequence.

## Relationship to existing work

Build on W2-135 body generations and write leases, W2-140 Project Session succession, W2-156 CI observation, and W2-123 visible-state semantics. Do not duplicate their models. If a required primitive is missing, extend its owning shared API in this Task's serial PR sequence and record the dependency.

## Exclusions

Do not pop or delete existing stashes, discard dirty work, create a second supervisor/store, or redesign GitHub review policy. Do not make canonical main writable by Project turns merely to bypass the read-only boundary.

task.name: [retired] Wake a waiting Task into ci-fix when its PR fails
task.description:
User story

After a Task opens a PR, it sleeps without consuming a provider body while required checks are pending. If a required check fails on the current PR head, Loopflow wakes that same durable Task into a bounded `ci-fix` turn, repairs the existing branch, and updates the same PR. The user does not discover CI failures manually or rescue the worker from its worktree.

Lifecycle contract

* Pending checks are healthy waiting: persist the PR, head SHA, check state, and freshness, but run no provider body.
* A required check transitioning to failed on the current head enqueues one audited `ci-fix` turn for the same Task Session, worktree, provider history, and active PR sequence. Include PR number/URL, branch, head SHA, failing check names, and log URLs so the skill resolves the exact failure.
* Coalesce simultaneous failures and deduplicate wakeups by PR head plus observed failure set. A repeated poll or webhook delivery must not create two bodies or two fixes.
* The `ci-fix` turn follows the builtin skill: reproduce the latest failure, make the smallest correct fix, run targeted then proportional checks, and report an infrastructure or credential blocker rather than weakening tests.
* After a push changes the head SHA, return to sleep and watch the new checks. Green checks remain waiting for the configured review/merge action; a new failure may wake one new `ci-fix` turn.
* Manual `lf task resume ISSUE MESSAGE` remains a supported override for rebase or review feedback and must be consumed before the default open-PR waiting transition.
* Preserve the exactly-one-body/write-lease rules and expose pending, fixing, blocked, and green-with-next-owner truthfully through `lf status`.

Operational boundary

Use the existing Task event/command path and builtin `ci-fix` skill. Do not add a second CI worker identity, duplicate Task, new worktree, provider transcript, or CI-specific monitor store. GitHub check evidence is authoritative only for the PR current head; stale failures never wake work.

Proof

A deterministic integration harness opens a PR and proves: pending checks consume no body; one required failure starts exactly one `ci-fix` turn with canonical metadata; duplicate and multi-check deliveries coalesce; the fix pushes the same branch/PR and rearms observation for the new SHA; green CI does not wake a body; and an infrastructure failure produces an actionable blocker without code churn. Reproduce W2-144 generation 7 to prove a queued manual repair is incorporated once instead of being discarded because the PR is open.

## Infrastructure dependencies

The full done-whens remain open until these substrate tasks merge and their evidence is incorporated:

* W2-229 — deterministic failed-PR ci-fix lifecycle proof
* W2-230 — durable audited ci-fix command ledger
* W2-231 — actionable Blocked semantics for infrastructure failures
* W2-232 — bounded ci-fix settlement without generic gate re-entry

PR #967 may ship as an incremental Product slice; it is not task-completion evidence by itself.

User story

When a Task attempt is abandoned because its provider, process, or execution context is unsafe, the user can deliberately recover that same durable Task without losing its worktree, serial PR history, directives, or audit trail—and without Loopflow silently restarting terminal work.

* Integrate with the leased-body supervision model: automatic process recovery may replace a body, but terminal abandonment is never crossed automatically.
* Expose actionability in CLI and shared Now/Roadmap DTOs: recover, resume, start next PR, complete, or no legal action, with reason and owner.

task.name: Make lf roadmap the machine-wide view of planned work
task.description:
## User story

As the person conducting Loopflow, I can run one fast command and understand every durable piece of planned work across every Wave: what exists, what is underway, what is blocked, and what could be started next. I should not have to open Linear, query each Wave, or interpret process internals to understand the roadmap.

## Product vocabulary

* `lf status` is exclusively the live execution view: Wave residents, Project and Task bodies, runs, current commands, progress age, stalls, review waits, recovery, and attention. It answers what is happening now and whether it is healthy.
* `lf roadmap` is the durable intent view backed by the local on-disk PM snapshot: Waves, Projects, KRs, and every open Task. It answers what exists and what could be worked on. Live execution state may be overlaid on a roadmap item, but the roadmap never becomes the owner of that state.
* `lf pm` remains the Linear planning mutation and synchronization surface.
* Do not add `lf work` or `lf status --all` as competing roadmap vocabulary. Tighten existing `lf status` output when necessary so the boundary remains true.

## End-to-end experience

`lf roadmap` is global by default and accepts an optional Wave scope. Its human output groups Tasks by Wave and Project, then presents concise sections for Now, Needs attention, Available, and Later. Every Task row carries its identifier, title, plan rank, concise reason, next owner, and active PR. When a durable Task has a live Session, the row overlays the shared execution category and progress age from `lf status`. Unavailable evidence says unavailable; an unstarted Task is never confused with a dead process.

`lf roadmap --json` emits one machine-wide shared DTO for CLI, Mac, iOS, and Wave Chat. Consumers derive Now, Available, and roadmap lenses from the same snapshot rather than spawning one subprocess per Wave or rebuilding status rules independently.

## Implementation bounds

* Read the existing SQLite registry and PM snapshots locally. The command is deterministic and fast: no Linear sync, network request, or agent turn.
* Reuse existing per-Wave Project and Task snapshots where their contract is correct. Add one envelope rather than a parallel planning model or database.
* Batch process and tmux evidence once per query; do not perform one subprocess or liveness probe per Task.
* Consume shared supervision categories and progress evidence from [W2-135](https://linear.app/loopflow/issue/W2-135/make-session-bodies-leased-progress-aware-and-recoverable). If that contract has not landed, keep the first slice additive and integrate after rebase rather than inventing another status taxonomy.
* Treat [W2-141](https://linear.app/loopflow/issue/W2-141/research-unified-now-available-work-views) as product research input and provide the data contract consumed by [W2-131](https://linear.app/loopflow/issue/W2-131/show-the-all-wave-roadmap-and-launch-or-attach-work-from-chat) and the Mac roadmap surface.

## Proof

* On the real accumulated workspace, one `lf roadmap` invocation lists all open Tasks in Product, Infrastructure, and Intelligence with no per-Wave commands.
* A running Task, review-waiting Task, stalled or failed Task, dependency-blocked Task, ready unstarted Task, and evidence-unavailable Task each render distinctly with the correct next owner.
* `lf roadmap --wave product` is a scoped projection of the same global result.
* `lf roadmap --json` round-trips through Rust and Swift fixtures without defaults or silent fallbacks.
* `lf status` contains live execution and attention rather than the complete inactive roadmap; `lf roadmap` contains durable planned work and only overlays live evidence.
* Mac and CLI consume one roadmap snapshot and agree on classification for the same fixture.
* A measured real-workspace read has a named latency budget and avoids N-Wave and N-Task subprocess fan-out.
* Rust, Swift, migration, and smoke gates pass, and user docs teach `lf status`, `lf roadmap`, and `lf pm` by example without overlapping promises.

User story

When Loopflow launches and submits a Task, the resulting PR contains exactly the work authored for that Task—never an unpushed canonical-main commit, a sibling Task’s change, or hidden ancestry from a stale stack. A human can trust the PR range before review without reconstructing Git history.

Contract

* Place new Task worktrees from a fetched `origin/<default>` commit when a remote exists; record that exact base as durable Task/PR evidence. A repository with no remote falls back explicitly to local main.
* Treat canonical main ahead of its upstream as a control-plane violation and stop new placement before contamination spreads.
* Before publication, prove the recorded base is compatible with current `origin/main`, the branch contains Task-authored changes, and the proposed PR range matches `lf task changes`.
* Refuse a contaminated or ambiguous range before GitHub side effects, naming the foreign commits/files and the safe rebase or recovery action.
* Keep readable branch names as hints. Placement metadata, commit ancestry, and Task PR sequence are authoritative.
* Work with multi-PR Tasks: after each serial merge, the next PR starts from current origin/main while the stable Task worktree and history continue.

Proof

Integration tests reproduce an ahead-of-origin canonical main, a stale recorded base, a squash-merged parent, a no-remote repository, and a multi-PR continuation. Every safe case opens the intended minimal range; every unsafe case stops before push. In ten dogfood Task PRs, GitHub’s range, `lf task changes`, and the Task’s recorded base agree with zero manual commit dropping.

Original evidence retained: W2-132/#877 and W2-130/#882 both inherited a foreign canonical-main commit and required manual repair. The old W2-141 scratch-file claim is not an acceptance criterion: submit intentionally clears scratch, so range correctness must be proven from durable Task and Git evidence instead.

task.name: [retired] Make Session bodies leased, progress-aware, and recoverable
task.description:
Product thesis

A Wave, Project, or Task is durable intent. A runner, provider turn, tmux session, PID, and process group are disposable bodies that temporarily act for that intent. Users should never have to manage those bodies, but they must always be able to see whether durable work is advancing, why it is not, and what Loopflow will do next. Wave, Project, and Task Sessions must share one coherent supervision model across CLI, Mac, iOS, chat, prompts, and worker processes.

Evidence that this Task must absorb

* On 2026-07-14 three Claude bodies slept for more than four hours while their Tasks still reported running because a PID and tmux session existed.
* W2-132 previously produced two live Claude processes using one provider history and worktree. A status column was treated as a write lock.
* Project processes died while child Tasks continued, leaving the durable hierarchy and the process hierarchy in disagreement.
* Legacy Sessions without pinned execution context could not be relaunched safely. PR #882 correctly refused to guess.
* Terminal Project pursuit could not create a successor until PR #894 separated terminal history from current work.
* An unbounded SSH command held a turn indefinitely until PR #893.
* PR #889 found two liveness paths in one snapshot disagreeing about whether tmux existed.
* Partial Task creation, process restart, host restart, interrupt, abandonment, and external side effects all create boundaries where blind replay is unsafe.

Product contract

1. Durable Session identity owns intent, directives, history, budget, relationships, worktree, PR sequence, terminal intent, and pinned execution context. It never derives identity from a process body.
2. Every body generation has an explicit write lease: generation and lease token, process group, PID or tmux identity, provider session, pinned lf binary and store, start time, heartbeat, activity time, meaningful progress time, deadline, and terminal outcome.
3. Exactly one generation may write, spawn, advance the flow, or report completion for a Session. Launch adopts a healthy body. Supersession atomically revokes the old lease, reaps its entire process group, and only then starts the successor. Stale generations become read-only and exit.
4. Liveness and progress are different evidence. Persist the current flow step and command, last provider event, last durable mutation, activity age, progress age, and relevant deadline. A long command may be alive without producing output, but it must be named, bounded or explicitly extended, and interruptible.
5. Desired intent and observed body state stay separate. The shared state model must express Working, Stalled, Recovering, NeedsInput, Stopped, Failed, Terminal, and Unobservable without collapsing them into one status string. Every state names the evidence, next owner, and legal controls.
6. Recovery is automatic only at a proven replay-safe boundary. A body lost during an external side effect becomes control-uncertain or NeedsInput with the command and evidence preserved; Loopflow must not blindly repeat it. Terminal intent always wins and is never restarted.
7. Supervisors recover the same durable Session and provider history. They never create parallel intent as a recovery mechanism. Host and process restarts must converge through the same state machine.
8. The shared wire contract feeds CLI, Mac, iOS, chat, and the Now/Roadmap work views. Human surfaces show occasional clear updates and actionable state; detailed heartbeats and command evidence remain in audit. Use the existing database and append-only events, not a second monitor store.

Delivery shape

This is one multi-PR Task with one stable worktree and provider history. Begin with an ambitious scratch design that audits W2-135, W2-139, PRs #882, #889, #893, #894, and the current supervisor and harness implementations. Write a one-screen user model, shared data types, a state-transition table, recovery policy, and serial PR boundaries before production changes. Keep one implementation across Wave, Project, and Task Sessions; do not add a Task-only watchdog beside existing supervision.

Expected serial slices are: shared supervision and wire model; atomic generation/write lease and process-group ownership; progress lease plus safe recovery; cross-surface status and controls; deterministic end-to-end dogfood. Adjust the boundaries when the code proves a simpler sequence, but preserve the single product model.

Proof

* A fake provider that stays alive but makes no meaningful progress becomes Stalled under a deterministic test clock, with current step or command and progress age visible.
* Safe recovery reaps the entire old process group and resumes the same Session, worktree, provider history, and pinned context at generation plus one. Sampling proves live writers never exceed one.
* A process or host restart adopts a valid body or recovers the same Session without duplicating work.
* A lost body during an uncertain external side effect becomes NeedsInput and is not replayed.
* Abandoned, completed, submitted, and otherwise terminal intent never restarts.
* CLI and Swift DTO fixtures expose the same evidence, category, reason, next owner, and controls.
* One intentional real dogfood stall is detected and recovered without a human discovering it from elapsed wall time.
* Full Rust, Swift, migration, and smoke gates pass for each relevant slice.

This Task absorbs W2-139. W2-144 and its Now, Available, and Roadmap consumers should depend on this unified contract rather than inventing another liveness model.

task.description:
## Outcome

A human and one real running Wave converse in one existing company Discord channel. A human message becomes durable Wave input, the Wave response appears in Discord, and a listener restart loses or duplicates neither side.

> "the wave is basically the stand in for the human, offering judgment and direction."

## Contract

* Discord is the canonical shared chat; Loopflow retains the external reference and exact Run input/output for evidence, not a second company transcript.
* Bind one explicitly configured existing guild channel to one Wave. Do not provision categories, shared rooms, threads, or wave-specific identities yet.
* The Wave listener owns polling, cursor, journal-first idempotent delivery, resident wake, and outbound receipt. The resident owns judgment.
* Initial binding starts at the current channel head. Thereafter restart catches up after the last committed message.
* Deduplicate inbound messages by provider/channel/message identity. Record outbound intent before send and reconcile the provider message ID after send.
* Read the Discord token only from Doppler/env. Never print it or pass it into provider children.
* Use only permissions exercised here: view channel, read history, read message content, and send messages.
* Do not restore the deleted generic bus or add Gateway machinery before polling load proves it necessary.

Post "summarize your current objective" in the bound channel and watch the real Wave answer. Restart its listener, post a second message, and receive one response. The trace shows exactly two source-linked human inputs and their assistant outputs. Tests cover first attach at head, ordered catch-up, duplicate fetch, crash between journal and cursor, outbound send reconciliation, self-echo rejection, missing permissions, and secret scrubbing.

task.name: One repository owns one Linear team across all of its Waves
task.description:
Intent

“Specifically, I want to make it so that each repo gets one team, so we'll have LOO for Loopflow. And then just put the wave name in each project so that it's obvious what the project is part of. This also makes sense for potentially larger nesting of waves because if you want to have a large nesting I don't think you want a lot of teams.”

Change the Linear sizing invariant from one Team per Wave to one Team per repository.

Target model

* Repository: one stable Linear Team and issue-key namespace.
* Wave: one Linear Initiative and durable operating context; Waves may be nested without creating Teams.
* Project: exactly one Wave-owned measured bet. Its visible Linear title includes the canonical Wave path.
* Task: one Linear issue on the repository Team, resolved to its Wave through its exactly-one Project relationship rather than through Team ownership.

Examples

* Loopflow repository Team: LOO.
* Hootro repository Team: HOO.
* Project title: Survival — A real task reaches done.
* Nested project title: Survival / Infrastructure — Gmail.

The title path is redundant human orientation, not the source of truth. Stable IDs and Initiative/Project associations remain authoritative. Use the canonical Wave ancestry so equal leaf names in different branches remain legible.

Constraints

* A repository may bind only one Linear Team. All of its Waves reuse that binding.
* Two different repositories must not silently claim the same Team.
* A Project still belongs to exactly one Wave even though its Team no longer identifies the Wave.
* Task and Project resolution must remain deterministic from UUIDs and Project membership.
* Existing Wave nesting, status, roadmap, task execution, PR lifecycle, and worktree ownership must not depend on unique Team prefixes.
* Repo-scoped PM authority should have one durable configuration owner rather than duplicated per-Wave values that can drift.
* Partial rollout must fail closed; do not leave some commands resolving Wave by Team while others resolve by Project.

Demo

In one fixture repository, initialize two sibling or parent/child Waves against one Team key. Create one Project under each, see Wave-qualified titles, create Tasks that share the same issue prefix, and resolve each Task back to the correct Wave through status, roadmap, task run, and project controls. A second repository attempting to claim the same Team is refused actionably.

Done when

* The repository-to-Team invariant is represented durably and validated by pm init, sync, project/task creation, resolution, and doctor surfaces.
* Multiple Waves in one repository share one Team without ambiguity.
* Project titles include canonical Wave paths, including nesting.
* Task-to-Wave resolution uses exactly-one Project ownership, not exclusive Team ownership.
* The full Wave-resolution and PM lifecycle test matrix covers same-repo sharing, nested Waves, cross-repo collision, duplicate Project association, restart, and migration compatibility.
* Documentation and recovery errors describe repository-scoped Teams consistently.

This is one architectural change: internal implementation may proceed in slices, but it should ship only when all planning and task consumers agree on the new invariant.

Problem

Review supervisors currently infer body health from indirect signals: whether the worktree changed and the last line visible in the tmux control pane. This can turn patient agent work into a restart loop.

Incident evidence: PRD-39 review ir_84622b87f9b047cb8a1261d74733eb56 on 2026-07-18.

* The control pane remained on `preparing launch prompt`, an info line emitted before prompt assembly at rust/loopflow/src/lf/commands/run.rs:169. Provider progress is not rendered there, so the line was stale presentation rather than current state.
* Codex generation 1 actively processed the review for 4m23s: it read review-design, the 394-line design, questions, and surrounding account code, and described the planned rewrite. The Project interrupted it before its first edit.
* Generation 2 actively processed for 2m32s, including context compaction and further source inspection, then was interrupted.
* Generation 3 actively processed for 2m16s, then was interrupted.
* All three provider rollouts ended with `turn_aborted: interrupted`; none emitted a provider failure.
* The Project nevertheless recorded `Codex launch prompt remained stuck` and handed the Task to OpenCode.
* OpenCode produced the rewrite after roughly six uninterrupted minutes. The difference was patience, not provider health.

Scope

Audit the complete reviewer decision surface: APIs, status projections, command receipts, event streams, attach/control output, and provider-neutral activity evidence. Determine whether Project and Wave reviewers receive enough timely information to distinguish queued input, prompt assembly, a working Turn, a quiet Turn, provider failure, and dead containment. Make supervision consume that truthful evidence.

Do not redesign the authored Review API or interaction protocol in this task. Treat that as a separate product effort; this task owns the evidence and liveness surface reviewers use when deciding whether to wait, message, interrupt, or hand off.

Done when

task.name: Delete Session and make Run the sole executor
task.description:
## Outcome

Finish the one-way cut begun by PR #1073. Wave, Project, and Task execution all use the shared Work -> Epoch -> Run -> Launch contract. ProjectSession and TaskSession stop being controller identities; Run is the only execution authority and Launch is the only provider/process lifetime. Provider conversation continuity remains a Launch resume token, not a Loopflow Session aggregate.

## Starting point

Base the work on merged main at PR #1073 (`ae1344a57`). `docs/architecture.md` is the design ledger. Update its moment-of-transparency first so shipped child-priority behavior and this remaining bridge are stated exactly. Make ambitious cross-cutting passes; do not preserve two controller stacks as a compatibility layer.

## Required cut

* Route Project and Task reserve, advance, wait, stop, interrupt, recovery, reaping, and completion fencing through one shared Run execution path keyed by `WorkRef`. Domain flows and closure checks remain explicit typed dispatch, not factories or generic registries.
* Keep stable Work and Epoch history across executor replacement. Run owns the exact opaque write lease. Launch owns PID/process group/tmux/provider route, containment, and optional resume token. Turn remains optional for opaque TUIs.
* Delete `ProjectSessionStatus`, `TaskSessionStatus`, `ChildWriteLease`, body generations, legacy Session authority environment variables, Session successor/controller identity, mirrored Run transitions, duplicate Project/Task runners and stores, and their DTO/CLI/Swift/schema surfaces. Do not delete provider resume continuity or terminal attach presentation merely because a vendor calls it a session.
* Make keeper recovery adopt or replace through Run/Launch evidence. Missing, stale, revoked, stopped, or foreign credentials fail closed; no ambient environment inference may become User authority. Interrupt targets the exact active Run/Launch and never falls back to Session lookup.
* Derive Work status, waits, review attention, controls, liveness, usage, and monitoring from Work/Epoch/Run/Launch/Turn plus domain truth. Preserve Project and Wave child-first lanes: direct User input first, then oldest child Review, then background cadence without losing the playhead.
* Preserve historical audit data only where it remains meaningful. Author the final one-way schema deletion as a draft migration under the release canonicalization contract; do not add a second registry or backwards-compatibility model.
* Update docs, builtins, fixtures, and tests in the same pass. Remove stale Session language from public product concepts while retaining explicit provider terminology where it describes reality.

## Behavior changes to prove

* Starting, waking, steering, interrupting, stopping, recovering, and completing Project and Task Work touch one authoritative Run state machine. Races with new Steer input cannot lose work or commit stale completion.
* A confirmed live Send records how delivery occurred but does not consume its Steer; a later Run/Turn Basis proves durable incorporation identically across Codex, Claude, OpenCode, and opaque tmux TUIs.
* A dead or unreachable process cannot remain a writer. Reaping requires positive containment evidence; unknown side effects remain explicit and are never blindly retried.
* A User-facing interactive review remains a live Launch even when the app is closed. Parent-agent reviews route through child attention and do not become a separate decision aggregate.
* Recovery after process or host restart preserves Work, Epoch, provider continuity when available, worktree, PR, outstanding Steers, and exactly-once child attention without reconstructing controller identity from Handles.

## Done when

1. Production code has zero Project/Task Session-controller types, tables, leases, generations, runners, or authority env vars; focused searches document any surviving vendor/UI use of the word session.
2. There is one Run reserve/advance/stop/recover path for Wave, Project, and Task, with typed Work dispatch only at domain behavior boundaries.
3. Behavioral tests cover exact authority, stale completion, input-vs-stop races, seed-only/live steering portability, keeper adoption/reaping, opaque TUI execution, restart, and child-first responsiveness.
4. Rust, migration, Python, Swift, UI compile, and E2E proofs pass; DTO fixtures remain lockstep with no defaults.
5. `docs/architecture.md` describes current reality without a temporary Session bridge.
6. Total repository source is at or below the documented 121,819-line ceiling, with deletion—not compatibility shims—accounting for the reduction.
7. The PR receives exact-head architectural review, lands from current main, and the live Product Wave can launch, steer, interrupt, recover, and finish a real Task through Run with no Session-controller record.
